caption_text: FIGURE 11.12. 1- to 2-Hz generalized periodic discharges (GPDs) in a 45-year-old female with acute-onchronic liver failure due to alcoholic cirrhosis. Note the triphasic morphology present with most discharges. Triphasic waves have three phases; (1) an initial negative phase, (2) a prominent positive phase, and (3) a final negative phase. Note the increasing duration of the three phases (i.e., phase 3 is longer than phase 2, which is longer than phase 1). Phase 1 or phase 3 might be of low amplitude or absent, and GPDs with triphasic morphology may both mimic nonconvulsive status epilepticus (NCSE) when they are continuous or represent NCSE in other cases (shown by clinical and EEG improvement after IV anti-seizure medication [ASM]). It can be quite challenging to determine which is the case in an individual patient. Although traditionally thought that GPDs with triphasic morphology suggested metabolic encephalopathy, blinded studies have called this association into question.
covered_aspects: 1–2 Hz GPDs with triphasic morphology in liver failure; NCSE mimic or NCSE
notes: b2_v3: GPDs as the broader ACNS category; triphasic morphology itself assigned to C0055
